context: The horizontal axis is input size n, marked from 1 to 14. The vertical axis is memory used and shows no numerical capacity scale. The chart illustrates growth trends. It does not compare actual byte counts or unscaled function values.
description: The table lists the curves from lowest to highest at their right ends, following the upward arrow labeled “Lower to higher, better to worse.”

frames.explanation: Some curves cross at small input sizes. For example, between 2 and 6 the logarithmic curve sits slightly above the linear one. The figure illustrates growth for sufficiently large n: constant space stays flat, logarithmic space grows slowly, and exponential space eventually grows fastest. The early intersections cannot tell us how much memory a particular input requires.
frames.title: Growth rates of common space complexities

summary: The chart compares how five space complexities grow as input size increases.

tables.caption: Five space complexities and their curve shapes
headers: Complexity (lowest to highest at the right edge)
rows: A green horizontal line just above the horizontal axis stays flat as n grows.
A cyan curve rises slowly and gradually flattens.
A straight blue line rises at a constant slope.
An orange curve bends upward and gets steeper.
A red curve stays near the bottom from about 1 to 8, then rises sharply.

title: Growth rates of common space complexities
